first.rationale: The current situation presents a convergence of signals: competitor price pressure on SMB segment, 6% activation decline, and 4% onboarding decline. Memory_73 directly addresses price-sensitive SMB acquisition and shows both revenue lift and reduced time-to-first-value—both critical metrics under competitive pressure. Memory_31 demonstrated that simplification drives activation, establishing a baseline for comparison. Verification of memory_73 is essential because pricing interventions carry material revenue risk and need confirmation of the magnitude and stability of the observed effect. Memory_31 verification provides control context on activation mechanics independent of pricing. Promotional pricing addresses the immediate competitive threat while supporting activation through faster value realization (per memory_73's documented time-to-value improvement). This preserves the referral and messaging levers (memories_57, memory_91) for follow-up if this experiment succeeds, avoiding premature saturation of growth tactics. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the current SMB-driven activation problem. Standard experiment scale balances risk against the need for decision speed in a competitive window; overly cautious approach risks continued share loss while the slot is available.
